faq.q: How efficient is a petrol engine?
faq.a: At its best, a modern petrol engine turns about 35 to 40 percent of the fuel's energy into work, but in everyday driving, with stops, idling and light loads, the average is nearer 20 to 25 percent. Diesel engines do a little better.
asks: What percentage of petrol energy moves the car?

faq.q: Why does so much energy go out of the exhaust?
faq.a: The burnt gases can only expand so far inside the cylinder before the exhaust valve opens, so they leave still hot and under some pressure. Turbochargers capture a little of this energy to squeeze more air into the engine.
asks: Why is a car exhaust hot?

faq.q: Why does a car engine need a radiator?
faq.a: Burning fuel heats the cylinder walls so much that the metal and oil would be damaged. Coolant carries the heat to the radiator, where air rushing through cools it.
asks: Why do car engines get so hot?

faq.q: Where does friction waste energy in an engine?
faq.a: Pistons rubbing in cylinders, spinning bearings, valve gear and oil pumps all turn some energy into heat. Pulling air in past a partly closed throttle also wastes energy, called pumping loss.

faq.q: Why are electric cars more efficient?
faq.a: An electric motor turns about 90 percent of its electrical energy into motion and can recover energy when braking. A petrol engine is a heat engine, so it must throw much of its energy away as heat.
asks: Are electric motors better than engines?

facts: In everyday driving, a typical petrol car turns only about a fifth to a quarter of its fuel's energy into motion.
The best modern car petrol engines reach a peak efficiency of around 40 percent.

quiz.say: In a typical car engine, roughly what share of the fuel's energy actually moves the car?
quiz.show: Share of petrol energy that moves the car?
quiz.why: Most of the energy leaves as heat in the exhaust and cooling system, leaving about a quarter to move the car.

wrong.1: Three quarters is roughly the share wasted as heat and friction.
wrong.2: No heat engine can turn all its fuel energy into motion.
